learning_outcomes.text: Acquire theoretical, methodological, and applied knowledge of Mathematical Analysis, enabling students to acquire the mathematical tools required for engineering applications.
Gain knowledge of the basic principles of differential calculus and integration theory for functions of one variable, and a range of applications will be presented.
Develop the ability to apply mathematical methods to model, analyse, and solve problems.
Develop the ability to analyse problems, identify different solution methods, and select the most appropriate approach.
Enhance learning skills and the ability to make independent judgements through independently solving a wide range of problems and exercises, followed by their correction and discussion.
Develop communication skills by presenting the topics covered and using the specialised language of foundational disciplines.

syllabus_topics: The set of real numbers and its properties
Complex numbers: algebraic, polar, and exponential forms
Functions of a real variable and limits of real-valued functions
Differential calculus for functions of one real variable
Integral calculus for real-valued functions: definite integrals and their properties
Indefinite integrals and methods of integration

assessment_methods.method: Online test with questions about prerequisites

assessment_rules: Students will be admitted to the written examination only after passing the online preliminary test on the course prerequisites. They may proceed to the oral examination only after passing the written examination. Both examinations are deemed to have been passed only if the student achieves a minimum mark of 18/30. The final grade is determined through a comparative assessment of the written and oral examinations. Honours are awarded for exceptional ability and independence of thought.
